A multinational corporate bank: Banking margins live between risk and speed: approve too slowly and the customer leaves, approve too fast and the losses follow. The Achala program started where that tension is sharpest —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
Periodic-review files queued for months; analysts spent 70% of their time assembling documents, not judging risk.
Registry extracts, screening results and account history lived across nine systems with no case context. Audit demanded evidence of review rationale; file histories were email archaeology.

KYC Management System agents now assemble each review file, registries, screening, financials, relationship notes, under a defined policy limit that routes only genuine judgment calls to analysts. The evidence trail (who saw what, when, why) is written as the work happens, and the risk-data spine on Forge keeps customer master data clean enough for the agents to trust.
